gaps.sentence: Does the project need ___ more work?
gaps.explanation: 'Work' is uncountable here, so 'much more work' is correct; 'many more work' is impossible.

gaps.sentence: A ___ of people object to the plans.
gaps.explanation: 'A large number of people' is correct for countables; 'a great deal of people' and 'an amount of people' are wrong.
'Several charges' means more than two; the other options are used only with uncountable nouns.

gaps.sentence: ___ of the two proposals has been approved so far.
gaps.explanation: 'Neither of the two' — 'none' is for three or more.

gaps.sentence: There are too ___ tourists in Venice in August.
gaps.explanation: 'Too many' is used before countable plurals like tourists; 'too much' is for uncountables.

gaps.sentence: ___ time I visit Rome, I discover something new.
gaps.explanation: 'Every time I ...' introduces repeated occasions; 'all time' and 'whole time' are not used here.
'Warm enough' means sufficiently warm; 'enough' follows the adjective.

gaps.sentence: There were ___ than twenty people at the meeting.
